summary: Appeals challenged the Kerala High Court's affirmation of convictions under IPC Sections 143, 147, 148, and Section 3(2)(e) of the Prevention of Damages to Public Property Act, read with Section 149 IPC, for a 2000 protest-turned-violence causing damage to 81 KSRTC buses and the death of a bus conductor, Rajesh. Central issues included the validity of Test Identification Parades (TIPs), allegations of police manipulation (pre-TIP exposure, photography, video-graphing, witness coordination during remand), and sufficiency of evidence for conspiracy and murder. The prosecution relied on witness testimony, including PW-68 for conspiracy, who was later disbelieved by the High Court. The Sessions Court convicted several accused, but the High Court acquitted Accused Nos. 1-2 and 25-33 of conspiracy due to lack of reliable evidence. The Supreme Court examined TIP procedures and evidentiary reliability.
legal_provisions_cited: Section 3(2)(e) Prevention of Damages to Public Property Act, 1984
final_judgment: The Supreme Court set aside the High Court's acquittal of Accused Nos. 1-2 and 25-33, restoring their conviction under Section 120B IPC r/w Section 3(2)(e) of the PDPP Act, Sections 109 and 111 IPC, after finding the Test Identification Parades valid and the evidence sufficient to support the conspiracy charge. The appeals were partly allowed, and the conviction and sentence of four years' rigorous imprisonment were upheld.
